Mayor DeGress in the Chair
Roll called and the following members
answered

Called Meeting of City Council
October 24th 1874
Council called to order at 8 oclock
P.M. Mayor DeGress in the Chair
Roll called and the following members
answered
Aldermen Cook, Deffenbaugh, James,
Maas, Robinson, Taylor and Witkins
Absent Aldermen Bremond, Darmour
and Ward. Quorum present.
The Mayor informed the Council that he
had called them together for the purpose of presenting to them his annual report as
required by city Ordinances.
Mayors Report
Mayor's Office Austin Texas
October 20th 1874
To the
Hon Board of Aldermen
City of Austin


 --- Page break --- 

351

Gentlemen

In compliance with Article 34 of the
City Ordinances, I have the honor to submit herewith my annual report.

Amount of Warrants outstanding Oct 20th 1877 $3,849.94 Bonded indebtedness of the City
June 9th 1877 95,900.00
Bonds sold since June 9th 1877 2,000.00
Total bonded indebtedness October
20th 1877 $97,900.00

The $2000 bonds sold by me was by authority of the City Council for the purpose of paying
Warrant No 638 amounting to $1834.50 including interest, also interest on Warrants No 639.
These Warrants were issued by Mayor Wheeler to the Silsby Manufacturing Company for one of
their fire engines

Cash in Treasury October 20th 1877 $3,038.35 Taxes uncollected for years prior to 1876
11,959.53
Taxes uncollected for 1876 4,796.24
Taxes uncollected for this year (1877) 55,544.79

By reference to the final report of Hon T.
B. Wheeler, it will be seen that the amount of Warrants outstanding on June 9th 1877, the
day of his retire- ment from the Office of mayor was $9,758.12, of which amount $2200 is
bearing ten per cent interest annually In addition to the above, warrants have been issued
by me amounting to $3,079.81¾ for work done under Mayor Wheeler's administration. All
these warrants are included in the above statement of $3,849.94 of warrants outstanding
October 20th 1877

Inventory of property belonging to the City
Two Engine Houses $3,051.00
Two Steam Fire Engines 13,000.00
One Fire Extinguisher 2,778.00
One Hand Fire Engine (cost $800) 500.00
One Horse Carriage Washington Hose Co No 1 250.00
Two thousand feet of Hose 2,500.00
Two Hook and Ladder Trucks 3,000.00
Furniture in Engine Houses 300.00
Market House and improvements 16,616.29
Steam Pumps 1,500.00
One Clock 1,200.00
Furniture of Court rooms and Offices including two Sofas 625.00 Horses, Mules, Carts,
Harness, Tools &c 850.00
Small pox hospital 618.5[illegible]


 --- Page break --- 

352
Hospital Block 2.215.20
Total $46,004.03
All work on streets and bridges has been paid for to date also for 603½ square yards of
guttering on Pecan Street less 20 per cent retained until the entire work is completed.
All the improvements of the streets except on Cedar and East Pecan streets have been made
with the prisoners of the City, and the streets have been kept in as good condition as the
working force at the command of the City would permit.
The City gained the suit against Duddington and Ducksinger for taxes due by them to the
amount of $550but the money collected from the parties has to be paid to parties now
holding a Judgement against the City.
I respectfully submit herewith a letter of the Assessor and Collector upon the subject
marked "A" I also call the attention of your honorable body to the detailed statement of
the City Clerk of the financial condition of the City marked "B"
I have no recommendations to make as the
terms of Office of the City Administration will expire in a few days
Very Respectfully
J. do. De Gues.
Mayor
Alderman Taylor moved that the report of
the Mayor together with the accompanying papers be received adopted and published in the
Statesman and Gazette and in one of the German papers Carried On motion of Alderman Moses
the report was ordered printed in the German paper published by Em Buchner
Petition of J.G. Woods for permission to
establish a Wood Yard in Vacant lot back of the City Hotel and to locate thereon an Engine
for the purpose of cutting wood for custom trade On motion of Alderman Watkins the
petition of
Mr Woods was laid on the table
Petition of Driskall. Day & Ford. D.L.Campbell H.T. Moore and others asking that a bridge
be built over the gutter on south side of Pecan Street at the crossing of the Utah
Railroad leading to the Central


 --- Page break --- 

353

Defect
On Motion of Alderman Taylor the petition was received and granted and the Street
Committee authorized to have the bridge constructed as soon as practicable The following
petitions were received, asking for license for the retailing of Spirituous Vinous and
malt liquors in quantitiesless than one Quart.
Johnson & co cor of Cedar + Lavaca Sts in Ward # 1
E. M. Brennan Congress Avenue " 9
J. Park, on Red River + Hickory St " 8
Chas Miller Congress Avenue " 8
Tho Severs " " 8
On Motion of Alderman James the above
petitions were granted
By City Attorney An Ordinance to license certain Vehicles used in the transportation of
persons for the period of One Week and establishing the rates thereon
The Ordinance was read.
Alderman Taylor moved to amend by inserting in the blank the following. For One horse
Vehicle One dollar per week. For two horse Vehicle One dollar and fifty cents per week.
For four horse Vehicle Two dollars and fifty cents per week Carried The Ordinance as
amended was read and passed to second reading Alderman Taylor moved to suspend the rules
and put the Ordinance on its second reading.
The Yeas and nays ordered and the motion to suspend the rules carried by the following
vote Yeas Aldermen Cook, Diffenbaugh James, Moore, Robinson Taylor and Withers Nays Stone
The Ordinance was read the Second time and passed to third reading
Alderman Robinson moved to further sus-
pend the rules and put the ordinance on its third reading The Yeas and Nays ordered and
the motion to further suspend the rules carried by the following vote Yeas Aldermen Cook,
Diffenbaugh, James, Moore, Robinson, Taylor and Withers. Nays Stone
The Ordinance was read the third time
Alderman Robinson moved that the Ordinance do pass The Yeas and Nays ordered and the
Ordinance


 --- Page break --- 

354

passed by the following Vote
Geas Aldermen Cook, Diffenbaugh James
Maas Robinson Taylor and Withers
Nays None
On motion of Alderman Withers
the Council adjourned
John L. [illegible]
City Clerk

Called Meeting of City Council
November 10th 1897
Council called to order at 4.30 P.M. Mayor
De Shew in the chair
Roll called & the following numbers
answered.
Aldermen Premond, James Maas Robinson
Taylor, Ward & Withers
Absent. Aldermen, Cook, Diffenbaugh
& Larmour. Quorum present.
The Journals of the Meetings of Oct 12-13& 27 were read and approved.
The Mayor stated that he had called the
Council together in compliance with article no.
116 of the City Ordinances & to transact such other business as may be presented.
The City Attorney submitted a detailed report of the Official business he had attended to
during the month. also regarding the garnishment in case of Walton & Shelley.
On motion of Alderman Ward the report
was read, and adopted
Petition of Cronin & Jones asking that their lease from the City for the old Miller
property be extended to 25 years. On motion of Alderman Ward the petition was referred to
the incoming administrators
